references.text: God's covenant with Abraham includes the command to circumcise all males as a sign of the covenant. Jacob's sons use this requirement in Genesis 34:15 as a condition for the marriage agreement with Shechem, but as part of a deception.

Abraham performs circumcision on himself, Ishmael, and all the males in his household, in obedience to God's command. In Genesis 34:15, Jacob's sons demand that all the males in Shechem's city be circumcised as well, but with deceitful intentions.
The verse explains that Jacob's sons answered Shechem and Hamor with deceit (במרמה), which provides the crucial context that the circumcision requirement in verse 15 was intended as a trap.
Shechem and Hamor accept the demand for circumcision and persuade the men of the city to be circumcised, which is the direct follow-up to the requirement in verse 15.

Joshua circumcises the Israelites at Gilgal after their wilderness journey, another account of mass circumcision that can be compared with the requirement that all males be circumcised in Genesis 34:15.
Direct continuation of the same dialogue where the condition for becoming one people (circumcision) is confirmed.
